# Overview

In this tutorial, we work through a complete multimodal regression workflow using **BayesCOOP**.

**BayesCOOP** is a scalable Bayesian framework for supervised multimodal integration with continuous outcomes. It uses group spike-and-slab double exponential shrinkage prior for joint feature/view selection and can optionally run a Bayesian bootstrap for uncertainty. For further details, see our [preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.684056v1).

In this tutorial we: (1) load and preprocess a longitudinal pregnancy
multi-omics dataset (immune + proteomics), (2) fit BayesCOOP with and
without Bayesian bootstrap, (3) compare against a frequentist cooperative
learning baseline, and (4) assess feature selection sparsity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Package Setup

We assume **BayesCOOP** is already installed in your R library.

```{r load_BayesCOOP}
library(BayesCOOP)
```

Now we load the packages used in this tutorial:
`MultiAssayExperiment` for multimodal data handling and `multiview` for
frequentist cooperative learning comparison.

```{r packages}
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(multiview)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Load the Pregnancy Dataset

We load the pregnancy dataset from local package data files in
`inst/ext_data` and convert it to `MultiAssayExperiment` objects for
downstream modeling.

```{r load_data}
list_to_mae <- function(dat, y_col = "Y") {
  if (!all(c("feature_table", "sample_metadata", "feature_metadata") %in% names(dat))) {
    stop("Input list must contain feature_table, sample_metadata, and feature_metadata.")
  }
  if (!all(c("featureID", "featureType") %in% colnames(dat$feature_metadata))) {
    stop("feature_metadata must contain featureID and featureType.")
  }
  if (!(y_col %in% colnames(dat$sample_metadata))) {
    stop("sample_metadata must contain the response column Y.")
  }

  feature_table <- as.matrix(dat$feature_table)
  feature_metadata <- dat$feature_metadata
  sample_metadata <- dat$sample_metadata

  feature_metadata <- feature_metadata[match(rownames(feature_table), feature_metadata$featureID), , drop = FALSE]
  if (any(is.na(feature_metadata$featureID))) {
    stop("Each feature row in feature_table must have a matching entry in feature_metadata$featureID.")
  }

  modalities <- as.character(feature_metadata$featureType)
  assays <- lapply(unique(modalities), function(mod) {
    feature_table[modalities == mod, , drop = FALSE]
  })
  names(assays) <- unique(modalities)

  common_samples <- Reduce(intersect, c(list(rownames(sample_metadata)), lapply(assays, colnames)))
  sample_metadata <- sample_metadata[common_samples, , drop = FALSE]
  assays <- lapply(assays, function(mat) mat[, common_samples, drop = FALSE])

  MultiAssayExperiment::MultiAssayExperiment(
    experiments = assays,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_metadata)
  )
}

## Load train/test data from inst/ext_data
data_candidates <- c(
  system.file("ext_data", package = "BayesCOOP"),
  file.path("inst", "ext_data"),
  file.path("..", "inst", "ext_data"),
  file.path("..", "..", "inst", "ext_data")
)

train_name <- "StelzerDOS.RData"
test_name <- "StelzerDOS_valid.RData"

data_dir <- ""
for (cand in data_candidates) {
  if (identical(cand, "")) {
    next
  }
  train_file_cand <- file.path(cand, train_name)
  test_file_cand <- file.path(cand, test_name)
  if (file.exists(train_file_cand) && file.exists(test_file_cand)) {
    data_dir <- cand
    break
  }
}

if (identical(data_dir, "")) {
  stop(
    "Missing required files: ", train_name, " and ", test_name,
    ". Expected under inst/ext_data (searched: ",
    paste(data_candidates, collapse = ", "), ")."
  )
}

train_file <- file.path(data_dir, train_name)
test_file <- file.path(data_dir, test_name)

data_train_list <- get(load(train_file))
data_test_list <- get(load(test_file))

## Convert to MultiAssayExperiment
data_train <- list_to_mae(data_train_list)
data_test <- list_to_mae(data_test_list)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Preprocessing

We remove metabolomics features since it is not present in the validation
set. Then we consider baseline samples only, ensuring that all assays and
outcomes stay synchronized across datasets. The data stay in MAE format
throughout.

```{r preprocess_data}
## Keep shared assays and remove Metabolomics
shared_assays <- intersect(
  names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_train)),
  names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_test))
)
shared_assays <- setdiff(shared_assays, "Metabolomics")

if (length(shared_assays) < 2) {
  stop("At least two shared assays are required for BayesCOOP.")
}

data_train <- data_train[, , shared_assays]
data_test <- data_test[, , shared_assays]

## Harmonize samples within each MAE
data_train <- MultiAssayExperiment::intersectColumns(data_train)
data_test <- MultiAssayExperiment::intersectColumns(data_test)

## Keep baseline samples only: train IDs containing 'A', test IDs containing 'G1'
train_ids <- grep(
  "A",
  rownames(MultiAssayExperiment::colData(data_train)),
  ignore.case = TRUE,
  value = TRUE
)
test_ids <- grep(
  "G1",
  rownames(MultiAssayExperiment::colData(data_test)),
  value = TRUE
)

data_train <- data_train[, train_ids, ]
data_test <- data_test[, test_ids, ]

## Filter features assay-wise, then keep common train/test features per assay
filter_assay <- function(assay_mat, abd_threshold = 0, prev_threshold = 0.1) {
  assay_df <- as.data.frame(t(assay_mat))
  assay_df <- BayesCOOP:::filter_features(
    assay_df,
    abd_threshold = abd_threshold,
    prev_threshold = prev_threshold
  )
  t(as.matrix(assay_df))
}

train_assays <- lapply(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_train), as.matrix)
test_assays <- lapply(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_test), as.matrix)

abd_thresh <- 0
prev_thresh <- 0.1
train_assays <- lapply(
  train_assays,
  filter_assay,
  abd_threshold = abd_thresh,
  prev_threshold = prev_thresh
)
test_assays <- lapply(
  test_assays,
  filter_assay,
  abd_threshold = abd_thresh,
  prev_threshold = prev_thresh
)

for (assay_name in names(train_assays)) {
  common_features <- intersect(
    rownames(train_assays[[assay_name]]),
    rownames(test_assays[[assay_name]])
  )
  train_assays[[assay_name]] <- train_assays[[assay_name]][
    common_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  test_assays[[assay_name]] <- test_assays[[assay_name]][
    common_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}

## Replace assays in MAE objects and keep MAE inputs for BayesCOOP
data_train_processed <- data_train
data_test_processed <- data_test
MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_train_processed) <-
  MultiAssayExperiment::ExperimentList(train_assays)
MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(data_test_processed) <-
  MultiAssayExperiment::ExperimentList(test_assays)

data_train_processed <- MultiAssayExperiment::intersectColumns(data_train_processed)
data_test_processed <- MultiAssayExperiment::intersectColumns(data_test_processed)

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Fit BayesCOOP (Bayesian bootstrap enabled)

Here we fit BayesCOOP using `bb = TRUE` to enable Bayesian bootstrap–based uncertainty estimation. This step may take a while because it involves multiple bootstrap iterations, which can be adjusted through the `bbiters` and `bbburn` parameters. The output includes the posterior samples of the parameters and runtime.


```{r fit_bb_true}
set.seed(123)

## Fitting BayesCOOP
fit_BayesCOOP_bb_true <- BayesCOOP(data_train = data_train_processed,
  family = "gaussian",
  ss = c(0.05, 1),
  group = TRUE,
  bb = TRUE,
  alpha_dirich = 1,
  bbiters = 100,
  bbburn = 50,
  maxit = 10,
  warning = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  control = list()
)

## Prediction
pred_BayesCOOP_bb_true <- predict(object = fit_BayesCOOP_bb_true,
                                            newdata = data_test_processed, family = "gaussian",
                                            bb = TRUE, warning = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

## Calculating mean squared prediction error
mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_true <- mean((pred_BayesCOOP_bb_true$y_pred - pred_BayesCOOP_bb_true$y_valid) ^ 2)
print(mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_true)
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Fit BayesCOOP (Bayesian bootstrap disabled)

We also run BayesCOOP again with `bb = FALSE` to obtain posterior mode estimates via a faster MAP-style variant (without bootstrap-based uncertainty). All other settings remain unchanged.
```{r fit_bb_false}
set.seed(123)

## Fitting BayesCOOP with `bb` = FALSE
fit_BayesCOOP_bb_false <- BayesCOOP(
  data_train = data_train_processed,
  family = "gaussian",
  ss = c(0.05, 1),
  group = TRUE,
  bb = FALSE,
  alpha_dirich = 1,
  bbiters = 100,
  bbburn = 50,
  maxit = 10,
  warning = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  control = list(rho = 0.5)
)

## Prediction
pred_BayesCOOP_bb_false <- predict(object = fit_BayesCOOP_bb_false,
                                            newdata = data_test_processed, family = "gaussian",
                                            bb = FALSE, warning = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

## Calculating mean squared prediction error
mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_false <- mean((pred_BayesCOOP_bb_false$y_pred - pred_BayesCOOP_bb_false$y_valid) ^ 2)
print(mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_false)
```


# 6. Cooperative Learning Baselines

Next, we construct three Cooperative Learning baselines using the
`multiview` package: "Early" (\eqn{\rho = 0}), "Intermediate"
(\eqn{\rho = 0.5}), and "Late" (\eqn{\rho = 1}). We apply identical
preprocessing steps, cross-validate the regularization parameter, fit the
models, and record the MSPE and runtime.

```{r cooperative_learning_baselines}
set.seed(123)

## Constructing the data for multiview implementation
y_train <- as.numeric(BayesCOOP:::gen_datalist(data_train_processed)$y)
y_test <- as.numeric(BayesCOOP:::gen_datalist(data_test_processed)$y)
xList_train <- BayesCOOP:::gen_datalist(data_train_processed)$xList
xList_test <- BayesCOOP:::gen_datalist(data_test_processed)$xList

## Matrix datatype conversion
xList_train <- lapply(xList_train, as.matrix)
xList_test <- lapply(xList_test, as.matrix)

## Choosing lambda using cross validation
cvfit_alpha <- function(xlist, y, rho, alpha = 1, folds = 5) {
  cvfit <- multiview::cv.multiview(
    x_list = xlist,
    y = y,
    rho = rho,
    alpha = alpha,
    nfolds = folds
  )
  list(lambda_min = cvfit$lambda.min)
}

## Different rho values for choice of fusion schemes
rhos_to_try <- c("Early" = 0, "Intermediate" = 0.5, "Late" = 1)
coop_results <- lapply(names(rhos_to_try), function(label) {
  rho_val <- rhos_to_try[[label]]
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  cvres <- cvfit_alpha(xList_train, y_train, rho = rho_val)
  best_lambda <- cvres$lambda_min
  fit_mv <- multiview::multiview(
    xList_train,
    y_train,
    lambda = best_lambda,
    rho = rho_val,
    alpha = 1
  )
  y_pred_mv <- as.numeric(
    predict(fit_mv, newx = xList_test, s = best_lambda)
  )
  mspe_mv <- mean((y_pred_mv - y_test)^2)
  runtime_min <- round(
    as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins")),
    3
  )

  coefs_mv <- coef(fit_mv, s = best_lambda)
  n_nonzero_mv <- sum(coefs_mv != 0) - 1

  list(
    method = label,
    rho = rho_val,
    mspe = mspe_mv,
    time_min = runtime_min,
    n_nonzero = n_nonzero_mv
  )
})
```

# 7. Performance Comparison

We next combine Mean Squared Prediction Error (MSPE) and runtime to assess
both accuracy and computational efficiency across models. Lower MSPE values
indicate better predictive performance.

```{r performance_comparison}
## Performance summary for BayesCOOP with `bb` = TRUE
BayesCOOP_bb_true_summary <- list(
  method = "BayesCOOP (bb=TRUE)",
  mspe = mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_true,
  time_min = fit_BayesCOOP_bb_true$time
)

## Performance summary for BayesCOOP with `bb` = FALSE
BayesCOOP_bb_false_summary <- list(
  method = "BayesCOOP (bb=FALSE)",
  mspe = mspe_BayesCOOP_bb_false,
  time_min = fit_BayesCOOP_bb_false$time
)

## Performance summary for multiview
coop_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(coop_results, function(res)
  data.frame(
    method = paste0(
      "Cooperative Learning (",
      res$method,
      ", rho=",
      res$rho,
      ")"
    ),
    mspe = res$mspe,
    time_min = res$time_min
  )
))

## Table for performance comparison
perf_table <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    method = BayesCOOP_bb_true_summary$method,
    mspe = BayesCOOP_bb_true_summary$mspe,
    time_min = BayesCOOP_bb_true_summary$time_min
  ),
  data.frame(
    method = BayesCOOP_bb_false_summary$method,
    mspe = BayesCOOP_bb_false_summary$mspe,
    time_min = BayesCOOP_bb_false_summary$time_min
  ),
  coop_df
)

## Print the performance table
print(perf_table)
```

# 8. Feature Selection / Sparsity Comparison

Finally, we count the number of selected (nonzero) features for each method
to compare their sparsity and selection aggressiveness.

```{r feature_selection_bcoop}
## Number of features selected for BayesCOOP with `bb` = TRUE
n_nz_BayesCOOP_bb_true <- sum(fit_BayesCOOP_bb_true$beta_postmed != 0)
## Number of features selected for BayesCOOP with `bb` = FALSE
n_nz_BayesCOOP_bb_false <- sum(fit_BayesCOOP_bb_false$beta_MAP != 0)
## Number of features selected for multiview
coop_sparse_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(coop_results, function(res)
  data.frame(
    method = paste0(
      "Cooperative Learning (",
      res$method,
      ", rho=",
      res$rho,
      ")"
    ),
    n_selected_feat = res$n_nonzero
  )
))

sparsity_table <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    method = "BayesCOOP (bb=TRUE)",
    n_selected_feat = n_nz_BayesCOOP_bb_true
  ),
  data.frame(
    method = "BayesCOOP (bb=FALSE)",
    n_selected_feat = n_nz_BayesCOOP_bb_false
  ),
  coop_sparse_df
)

## Print table comparing the number of selected features for different methods
sparsity_table
```

For this particular dataset, both BayesCOOP variants achieved lower MSPE
compared to their frequentist counterparts, with the Bayesian Bootstrap
version producing a more parsimonious model. For an in-depth biological
interpretation of the feature selection results, please check out our
[preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.684056v1).
